clue.text: Member of crew in readiness at close quarters

parts.note: a hand is a crew member or labourer, as in 'all hands on deck'
to hand means available and ready for use

explanation.surface: A sailor stands by, ready for action in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-to-hand fighting is combat at very close range, body against body.

clue.text: Daredevil, somehow pulled up short

indicators.note: pulled about somehow, so these letters are tugged into a new order

explanation.surface: A stuntman's act somehow comes to an abrupt halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow pulled' rearranges UP and SHORT to give the letters. Harry Hotspur was the rash young warrior of Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, impetuous person, from the nickname of the reckless Henry Percy.

clue.text: Modern and old currency used in Pacific Island

parts.note: modern means new
the guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: Notes old and new circulate on a South Seas island.
explanation.definitionFit: This large island north of Australia lies in the western Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Driving manoeuvre — it used to be worth a try

definitions.meaning: a way of reversing direction in a narrow road using forward, back and forward moves

definitions.text: it used to be worth a try
definitions.meaning: in rugby a try was once worth three points, and a try is also a go or turn

explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union tries were worth three points until 1971; 'a try' also means a go, so a three-point go is a three-point turn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard name for turning a car round in three moves on a narrow road.

clue.text: Poor actor's name finally dropped — one running round in circles?

parts.note: a ham is a poor, overacting actor; the 's gives S

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped off

parts.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A bad actor is cut from the credits and left running around aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dropped' removes the last letter, M, from TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet hamsters famously run endlessly round in exercise wheels.

clue.text: Losing heart, you never dance — he may have inspired you

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order
the word you loses its central letter

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: Someone who never dances is told a great ballet star might have inspired them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' takes O from YOU leaving YU, and 'dance' rearranges YU with NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev, the great ballet dancer, inspired many people to take up dance.

clue.text: Could they be evens? Yes and no

definitions.text: Could they be evens? Yes and no

parts.words: Could they be evens? Yes and no
parts.note: in betting, a price can be evens; but odd numbers are never even, so yes and no

explanation.walkthrough: Betting prices include 'evens', yet numbers that are not even are the opposite: both readings hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting prices are quoted as these, evens being one, while as numbers they are the opposite of even.

clue.text: Information turning up army is bogged down

annotationWithheld.why: Information turning up — army is bogged down (5): DATUM is TA inside MUD reversed, but 'bogged down' must supply MUD and also signal the container, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Information turning up army is bogged down

clue.text: Tell me to stop being a shy, new stranger

indicators.note: stranger read as more strange, so these letters take an odder order

explanation.surface: A timid newcomer is asked to say when to stop pouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for the newcomer but is the anagram signal on A SHY NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pouring a drink asks you to say when, meaning tell them to stop.

clue.text: Space is fantastic

definitions.meaning: outer space lies beyond the Earth

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are joined by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally beyond the Earth, and idiomatically marvellously good.

clue.text: Building a tug?

definitions.meaning: a tall structure such as a castle keep
a tug is a boat that tows, so whimsically one that tows

explanation.definitionFit: A tall building, and whimsically anything that tows, as a tugboat does.

clue.text: Handicraft — brand name attached to sample

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: A craftwork range is branded and offered for tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is the decorative craft of inlaying veneers of wood into furniture.

clue.text: Discreetly supply wrapping for obscene books

indicators.note: the first piece is wrapped around the others

parts.note: to ply someone is to supply them persistently
rude means obscene
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Dirty books are sent out tactfully in plain wrappers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' means the supply word is split around the others; 'books' for the New Testament is a standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting prudently means acting with caution and good judgement, discreetly.

clue.text: Sound of brass band doesn't have a lot of appeal

indicators.note: the named letter is left out

parts.note: oompah is the sound of a tuba-led brass band

explanation.surface: A brass band's sound lacks charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have' removes the A from OOMPAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is vigour or sex appeal, plenty of attractive energy.

clue.text: Spite soldier's voiced

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks

explanation.surface: A soldier speaks his malice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike; 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment or spite.

clue.text: Tax applied to one drink, perhaps, in this city

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
I is the Roman numeral one
a can contains a drink, or to can is slang for drink

explanation.surface: A tourist pays sales tax on a single drink in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is the papal city-state within Rome.

clue.text: Bird, fish or insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A list of creatures: a bird, a fish, or a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' looks like a choice of definitions; only 'insect' defines, with bird and fish the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a common scavenging insect.

clue.text: Thingumajig that now looks rather different

indicators.note: these letters, rearranged, look rather different

explanation.surface: A gadget that now has a new look.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is an unnamed thing, as is a thingumajig; also a stand of shelves.

clue.text: Element to spoil run up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read backwards from the bottom

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
to flow is to run

explanation.surface: An element ruins a run upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of MARFLOW backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a chemical element.

clue.text: Arbitrator gets work outside plant

indicators.note: the work word goes outside the arbitrator

parts.note: toil is hard work
a ref, or referee, arbitrates

explanation.surface: A referee finds a job beyond his pitch planting greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; 'outside' tells you the work word surrounds the referee, split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is clover or a similar three-leaved plant.

clue.text: Showed two guys embracing

indicators.note: one man's name holds the other inside

parts.note: Ed is a man's name
Vince is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men hugging made their feelings plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two guys' supplies two men's names; 'embracing' has the shorter name hugging the longer one.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or display a feeling clearly.

clue.text: Follows around right guarantees

indicators.note: the first word goes around the letter

parts.note: ensues means follows

explanation.surface: Sticking to the right way gives certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensures means makes certain, guarantees.

clue.text: Computer kept crashing with DOS

indicators.note: a crashing system jumbles everything, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A PC kept crashing under its old operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: DOS was an early PC operating system, here just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer designed to sit on a desk.

clue.text: Left one million, I start to take control

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: With a million left, I begin to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict or control it.

clue.text: Builder employing parent and child

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A building firm hires a mother and her son.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason builds with stone or brick.

clue.text: In a stewards' enquiry, its head takes the lead —- moving in this direction?

indicators.note: the head letter of enquiry moves to the front of the letters

parts.note: the words taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: At a racecourse inquiry, the leading horse's trainer is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of 'enquiry' (its head) is already in A STEWARDS; it moves from the middle to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastwards means towards the east, a direction of movement.

clue.text: Engineers attending the mechanism I run in store

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a servo is a control mechanism
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Army engineers look after the machinery in a depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store, especially of water.

clue.text: Criticise cook

explanation.definitionFit: To roast means both to criticise harshly and to cook in an oven.

clue.text: Source of wealth belonging to me

definitions.meaning: a pit yielding gold or coal
the possessive pronoun of the first person

explanation.definitionFit: A pit producing riches, and the first-person possessive pronoun.

clue.text: Ceased trading where union holds sway

definitions.meaning: a business that has closed its doors
a workplace where all staff must belong to a trade union

explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a firm requiring union membership, and literally a shut store.
